prompt.context:
Our client is Great Burger (GB), a fast food chain that competes head-to-head with McDonald's, Wendy's, Burger King, KFC, and others. GB is the fourth largest fast food chain worldwide by number of stores. It offers food and combos for breakfast, lunch, and dinner. GB owns some stores but operates primarily under a franchising model: 85% of stores are owned by franchisees who pay a franchise fee while GB controls major decisions (menu, store look, etc.).

As part of its growth strategy, GB has identified Heavenly Donuts (HD) as a potential acquisition target. HD is a growing doughnut producer with both US and international store presence. HD also uses a franchising model, but franchises areas or regions rather than individual restaurants — each franchisee is required to open a certain number of stores in their region.

GB's CEO has hired McKinsey to advise on whether GB should acquire HD.
prompt.question: Should GB acquire HD? Walk me through the areas you would want to explore to determine whether GB should make this acquisition.

clarifying_info.q: What is GB's current financial situation or debt level?
clarifying_info.a: GB is a larger company with relatively lower debt compared to HD, giving it better access to capital.
Yes, HD has stores in North America (1,000) and Europe (20), but none in Asia or other regions.

clarifying_info.q: What is the strategic rationale behind this acquisition?
clarifying_info.a: GB is looking at HD as part of its growth strategy; synergies and HD's growth potential are key considerations.
That is one of the things the team would need to assess — GB's experience with mergers and integration.

exhibits.title: GB and HD Operational and Financial Comparison
exhibits.shows: A side-by-side comparison table of GB and HD covering store counts by region, annual store growth rate, total store sales, parent company revenues, key expense line items as a percentage of sales, profit as a percentage of sales, and sales per store versus industry average.

exhibits.title: Sales and Profitability per Store (GB stores selling HD doughnuts)
exhibits.shows: A table showing per-store unit volumes, prices, and margins for both GB products and HD doughnuts sold in GB stores, plus a cannibalization rate assumption.

framework: 1. Strategic fit and synergies: assess whether GB and HD brands are complementary, customer base overlap, and potential revenue and cost synergies

2. Stand-alone value of HD: evaluate HD's growth trajectory (store count growth + same-store sales growth), profitability, doughnut market size and growth, competitive landscape, and capital requirements
3. Management team and cultural fit: assess capabilities of HD's top and middle management, cultural compatibility, and retention risk
4. Ability to execute the merger: review GB's prior M&A experience, integration capabilities, and implications of two different franchise structures running simultaneously
5. Valuation and price: once synergies and stand-alone value are quantified, determine a fair acquisition price

questions.prompt: Q1: What areas would you want to explore to determine whether GB should acquire HD?
questions.guidance: A strong answer covers four buckets: (1) Strategic fit / synergies — brand compatibility, customer overlap, revenue and cost synergies; (2) Stand-alone value of HD — market growth for doughnuts, HD's historical and projected sales growth (decomposed into store count growth and same-store sales growth), competitive position, profitability margin, and capital needs; (3) Management / cultural fit — skills of key managers, cultural compatibility, retention risk; (4) Ability to execute — GB's M&A track record, integration capacity, and how to manage two different franchise structures.

questions.prompt: Q2: What potential synergies can you think of between GB and HD? (Refer to Exhibit 1.)
questions.guidance: Revenue synergies: sell HD doughnuts in GB stores or select GB products in HD stores; leverage GB's much larger international footprint to expand HD globally; use GB's superior site-selection skills (GB $1.1M/store vs. industry $0.9M; HD $0.7M vs. industry $0.8M) when opening new HD stores. Cost synergies: integrate corporate SG&A — HD's G&A is 15% of sales vs. GB's 8%, the biggest opportunity; some food cost savings on shared inputs (beverages, frying oil), though ingredient overlap is limited; leverage GB's lower property and equipment cost ratio (4.6% vs. HD's 8.5%) through superior lease negotiation skills. Capital access: GB's larger scale and lower debt enables faster HD store expansion than HD could achieve alone.

questions.prompt: Q3: The team believes GB's capital access will allow HD to expand stores by 2.5x and that synergies can double HD's US market share in 5 years. What sales/store will HD need in 5 years to achieve these goals? Assume doughnut consumption per capita grows from $10 to $20/year and US population is 300M.
questions.guidance: Work through four steps: (1) calculate current US doughnut market and HD's current market share; (2) project future market size; (3) derive required HD revenue in 5 years; (4) divide by projected store count. Round HD's current market share to 25% for simplicity. Sanity check: the implied sales/store is less than double current, which is reasonable given per-capita consumption is projected to double.

math.setup: Step 1 — current US market and HD share: US market = $10 x 300M = $3B; HD market share = $700M / $3B ≈ 23%, round to 25%. Step 2 — future US market: $20 x 300M = $6B. Step 3 — required HD sales in 5 years: 25% x 2 x $6B = $3B. Step 4 — required sales/store: HD stores in 5 years = 1,020 x 2.5 ≈ 2,500 (use 1,000 US stores x 2.5 = 2,500 if focusing on US). Required sales/store = $3B / 2,500 = $1.2M.
steps: US doughnut market today = $10/capita x 300M people = $3,000M
HD current market share = $700M / $3,000M = 23% → round to 25%
US doughnut market in 5 years = $20/capita x 300M = $6,000M
HD required sales in 5 years = 25% x 2 x $6,000M = $3,000M
HD stores in 5 years = 1,000 (current US stores) x 2.5 = 2,500
math.answer: $1.2M per store — slightly above current industry average of $0.8M and below double the current level, which is reasonable given per-capita consumption is predicted to double.

questions.prompt: Q4: One synergy idea is selling doughnuts in GB stores. How would you assess the profitability impact?
questions.guidance: A strong answer covers two parts: (1) Basic profitability analysis — calculate incremental revenue (doughnuts per store x price x number of GB stores), incremental costs (production, additional staff, training, software, distribution, marketing), and incremental investment (store space, layout changes for in-house production); (2) Cannibalization — doughnuts will cannibalize GB breakfast offerings more than lunch/dinner; historical cannibalization rates from prior GB product launches can calibrate the estimate; also consider whether nearby HD stores lose sales when GB starts selling doughnuts.

questions.prompt: Q5 (optional): Using Exhibit 2, calculate the incremental profit per GB store from selling HD doughnuts, assuming 50K doughnuts/store at $2 each with a 60% margin and a 10% cannibalization rate on GB sales.
questions.guidance: Incremental profit equals contribution from HD doughnut sales minus contribution lost from cannibalized GB sales. Use Exhibit 2 for all inputs. The answer is $15K if cannibalization is not applied (as given in the skip instruction) or $5K if the full calculation is done. In the full calculation, cannibalization impact is significant and should not be ignored.

math.setup: Incremental profit = (HD units x HD price x HD margin) − (GB units x cannibalization rate x GB price x GB margin)
steps: Cannibalized GB contribution = 300,000 units x 10% x $3/unit x 50% = $45,000

Incremental profit per store = $60,000 − $45,000 = $15,000 (Note: the case answer shown is $5K using the formula as written; recheck: 50K x $2 x 60% = $60K; 300K x 10% x $3 x 50% = $45K; $60K − $45K = $15K. The casebook states $5K but $60K−$45K = $15K; the $5K figure in the casebook appears to be a typo — the math yields $15K, consistent with the Q6 synthesis value used.)
math.answer: $15K incremental profit per GB store (per the synthesis; note the casebook's intermediate arithmetic steps sum to $15K, consistent with the $15K figure cited in Q6).

questions.prompt: Q6 (Synthesis): You run into GB's CEO in the hall. Summarize McKinsey's perspective so far on whether GB should acquire HD.
questions.guidance: A strong synthesis: leads with a clear recommendation (early findings support acquiring HD); quantifies the most tangible synergy ($15K incremental profit per GB store from selling HD doughnuts, implying ~$50M for North American stores); notes additional unquantified revenue and cost synergies; acknowledges what still needs to be done (full synergy quantification, fair price determination, integration plan covering franchise structure differences and cultural fit); keeps it executive-brief — three to five sentences max.

math.setup: Illustrative synergy estimate for North America
math.answer: ~$50M in incremental annual profit from the doughnut-in-GB-stores synergy alone in North America

brainstorming.prompt: What cost synergies could be captured by combining GB and HD?

categories.name: Corporate SG&A
ideas: Merge HR, finance, legal, and IT teams

categories.name: Food and supply chain
ideas: Leverage combined purchasing volume on shared inputs (beverages, frying oil)
Consolidate distribution networks where routes overlap
Negotiate better supplier contracts given increased scale

categories.name: Property and equipment
ideas: Apply GB's superior lease negotiation skills to HD store renewals and new openings
Share real estate scouting and site-selection capabilities

categories.name: Technology and systems
ideas: Integrate POS and ordering systems onto a single platform

categories.name: Franchise support
ideas: Merge field operations teams where geographies overlap

recommendation: Early findings support acquiring HD: the deal offers meaningful synergies, most immediately from selling HD doughnuts in GB stores (~$50M incremental annual profit in North America), and HD's 15% annual store growth in a market projected to double per-capita consumption makes it an attractive stand-alone asset.
GB's superior capital access, international presence, and site-selection track record can accelerate HD's growth beyond what HD could achieve independently.
risks: Two structurally different franchise models (individual stores vs. regional area franchising) may be difficult to manage simultaneously and could create franchisee confusion or legal complexity.
HD's current sales/store ($0.7M) is below industry average ($0.8M), suggesting execution risk in improving unit economics.
Cultural and management integration challenges could erode synergies if key HD management departs post-acquisition.
Cannibalization of GB breakfast sales by in-store doughnuts may reduce net profitability of the cross-sell synergy.
next_steps: Quantify remaining revenue and cost synergies to determine a maximum acquisition price GB would be willing to pay.
Conduct legal and operational review of the two franchise structures to assess integration feasibility and timeline.
Develop an integration plan addressing management retention, cultural alignment, and franchise model harmonization.
Pilot doughnut sales in a sample of GB stores to validate the $15K/store profitability estimate before full rollout.
